notes.content: The BS in Nutrition and Food Sciences - General Dietetics Option is an approved match to the AS-T in Nutrition and Dietetics.
notes.contentHtml: The BS in Nutrition and Food Sciences - General Dietetics Option is an approved match to the AS-T in Nutrition and Dietetics.

notes.content: A supplemental dietetics application must be submitted by March 1. A dietetics application is available from the Nutrition and Food Sciences (NFSC) Department office. In addition to the application, students must provide: transcripts of all previous college or university level work, a resume, two letters of recommendation, one-page written personal statement about their career goals. Applications are reviewed by a committee that ranks all applications for placement. Students not selected for the option are encouraged to meet with a NFSC faculty advisor. Students not selected may reapply once.
notes.contentHtml:
A supplemental dietetics application must be submitted by March 1.

A dietetics application is available from the Nutrition and Food Sciences (NFSC) Department office.

In addition to the application, students must provide:

  1. transcripts of all previous college or university level work,
  2. a resume,
  3. two letters of recommendation,
  4. one-page written personal statement about their career goals.

Applications are reviewed by a committee that ranks all applications for placement.

Students not selected for the option are encouraged to meet with a NFSC faculty advisor.

Students not selected may reapply once.

notes.content: Prerequisites for Admission to the Option in General Dietetics

All required courses must be passed with a grade of C or higher. Progression in the option in general dietetics depends upon maintaining a cumulative grade point average of 2.75 and a grade of C or higher in all courses listed in the major core and in the option in general dietetics. The following prerequisites must be completed with a grade of C or higher: BIOL 104 , BIOL 211 , CHEM 107 , CHEM 108 , MATH 105 .

notes.content: Clinical Nutrition is not a requirement of the General Dietetics. Only students preparing for advanced degrees or careers in nutrition research should complete the required units of the Option in General Dietetics and also complete the courses listed below (only one course at the lower division level), which include a Chemistry minor.
